newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan opposition recaptures key Bagram airbase.
newsitem.headline: Afghan opposition recaptures key Bagram airbase.

text.p: Afghan opposition forces re-captured Bagram airbase, north of capital Kabul, on Friday night hours after losing it to the Islamic Taleban militia, a Pakistan-based Afghan news agency said on Saturday.
The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) said forces loyal to ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani drove out the Taleban from the airbase in a midnight attack in which three Taleban fighters were killed.
A Taleban spokesman confirmed that Bagram base, 50 km (30 miles) from Kabul, had been lost but said fighting was continuing in the area.
"We are still occupying strategic positions in the environs of Bagram airbase and fighting is continuing," the AIP quoted the Taleban spokesman as saying.
He said Taleban forces were in Asmatullah village close to the airbase. "Heavy fighting is going on," he added.
The spokesman said Taleban forces, which had captured the nearby opposition stronghold of Qarabagh from the forces of General Abdul Rashid Dostum, were now heading towards Charikar.
The Taleban forces entered Bagram on Friday evening after capturing Qarabagh after a day-long offensive.
AIP said at least 50 opposition fighters were killed and 230 captured in Qarabagh, including Abdus Sabur Farid of the Hezb-i-Islami party who briefly served as prime minister under Rabbani in 1993.

The Taleban had taken Qarabagh and Bagram immediately after capturing Kabul on September 27 but it was forced to withdraw after forces led by Rabbani's top military commander, Ahmad Shah Masood, counter-attacked.
Bagram was used by the Soviet occupation forces as the main airbase to fight mujahideen guerrillas in the 1980s and was later used by Rabbani's government to fight its opponents.
